subject: Follow-up: token budgets, concurrency & streaming constraints
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finval.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T14:15:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: token budgets, concurrency & streaming constraints

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick consolidated recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size a clean PoC. I copied Vivek and Marcus for the technical sizing.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary UX: interactive analyst chat with progressive streaming of partial answers.
- Latency target: you said ~150ms p95 for short exchanges, but you flagged tolerance up to 200ms for long-context responses.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~20 concurrent users (average), peak concurrent sessions ~60, and rare bursts up to ~200 for <1 minute at the end of quarter.
- Token profile (rough): typical user prompt ~2k input tokens, iterative follow-ups ~500 tokens, maximum single exchange output up to 1.5k tokens. Some workflows require reading a whole 20–30k doc (so long-context capability important).
- Streaming: required for analyst-facing experience (partial sentences must arrive as tokens are generated).
- Security: initial PoC can run on hosted Redwood API; long-term may require Dedicated or Private for audit requirements.

Open clarifications we need from you (please reply inline):
1) Confirm the p95 latency target you want us to optimize to for the PoC — 150ms or 200ms?
2) Confirm the portion of requests that will be long-context (>=16k tokens). Is this 5% / 20% / 50%?
3) Can you share a 24–48 hour sample of prompt lengths or a representative prompt set (we can use synthetic traffic if needed)?

What we propose for the PoC (high-level):
- 2-week bench: measure p50/p95 latency, token throughput (tokens/sec), and streaming deliverability across two modes: (A) frequent short exchanges (<=4k total tokens) and (B) long-context document reads (>=16k tokens).
- Start against hosted capacity with a recommended model variant; if we see tail pressure we'll move to a 4-GPU Dedicated pool for predictable SLOs.
- Instrumentation: token-level latency traces, KV cache hit rate, and billing estimate.

Attached: Redwood draft performance estimate, quick PoC plan, and a sample prompt set placeholder.

Next steps: please confirm the three clarifications above and your range for acceptable PoC SLOs. If you’re okay, we’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff Tue/Thu next week.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: token budgets, concurrency & streaming constraints

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline and a couple of extra data points.

1) Latency target: operationally we'd like 150ms p95 for the short/interactive flows. For the long-context document reads, 250ms p95 is acceptable as long as streaming starts producing partial answers in <120ms.
2) Long-context portion: today we expect ~15% of analyst queries to be long-context (>=16k). That can spike to ~30% when a user uploads a long report.
3) Sample data: attaching a small prompt dump and a sample doc (we'll upload a larger sample to your Drive link later).

Other clarifications:
- Peak burst tolerance: we can accept brief exceeded latency for infrequent bursts but want graceful degradation (fallback to a smaller model or queued streaming).
- Security: PoC on hosted is fine but we do require audit logs and retention controls (we can provide details to your security contact).

I'll loop in our infra contact if you need deeper logs. For scheduling, Tue 10–10:30 PT works.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Sharma

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T18:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: proposed PoC sizing & config suggestions

Hannah / Marcus — quick internal sketch based on Priya's responses. Key tradeoffs and suggested configuration: 

Observations:
- Streaming latency has two components: (1) token generation latency (compute + kernel time) and (2) network/transfer latency for small incremental chunks. For short exchanges we can hit ~120–160ms p95 on high-frequency tokens if we avoid large KV cache thrashing.
- Long-context (>=16k) increases memory pressure and KV lookup overhead; that typically pushes generation p95 into the 250–400ms range unless we use quantized kernels and GPU memory-optimized models.

Suggested PoC config:
- Start hosted with model family: redwood-open-13b-32k (quantized q4f16) to test correctness and streaming behavior.
- If PoC needs consistent 150ms p95 for short flows at their stated concurrency, plan Dedicated with 4x A100-class GPUs behind a low-latency routing tier. Autoscale policy: keep baseline 2 workers, scale to 6 on sustained 60+ concurrent sessions, with burst capacity to 12 for minute-scale spikes.
- Concurrency & batching: set per-worker concurrency limit to 8 generation streams, enable dynamic microbatching with a 5ms batching window for efficient throughput without hurting tail latency.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for frequently repeated prompts and turn on response caching for deterministic prompts to reduce cost and latency.

Bench plan & success criteria:
- Mode A (short): 10k synthetic requests, 2–10 tokens output typical, target p95 <=150ms and p50 <=60ms.
- Mode B (long): 1k requests with inputs 16k–32k tokens, streaming start latency <=120ms, p95 generation latency <=300ms.
- Monitoring: token-level traces, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, and per-request fallback count.

Risks to call out:
- If their long-context share spikes >30% we'll likely need a memory-optimized 70B model or split-encoding approach which increases cost.
- Network egress for streaming small chunks could dominate if clients are across regions — recommend colocating in us-west for PoC.

I'll attach a quick sample benchmark script and an updated estimate. Happy to pair on the kickoff.

Cheers — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

2) Success metrics we will instrument: Mode A p95 <=150ms, Mode B streaming start <=120ms and p95 <=300ms. We'll also report cost-per-1k tokens and KV cache hit rate.
3) Infra request: please add one infra contact to the Drive link so we can share audit-log sample payloads for their security team.
4) Billing/contact: who should we send the PoC cost estimate and potential Dedicated subscription quote to?
